chunks: From him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The pregnant woman whose husband dies, gives birth and remarries before the expiration of four months and ten days.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'If her husband, from whom she married, had consummated the marriage with her, separation is effected between them, and she observes the remainder of her first waiting period, and another waiting period from the latter one.'
And if he had not consummated the marriage with her, separation is effected between them, and she observes the remainder of her waiting period, and he is a suitor among suitors.'

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: He consummated the marriage (entered with her)

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a pregnant widow who remarries before giving birth?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural handling of 'iddah for a pregnant widow who remarries before the expiration of her first husband's waiting period, distinguishing rulings based on whether the first marriage was consummated. It establishes that if consummated, she completes the remainder of the first 'iddah and begins a new one for the second husband; if not, the second husband is treated as a suitor until the first 'iddah concludes. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of legal status and the specific duration of four months and ten days for pregnant widows.

en.hubeali: From him, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The pregnant woman widowed from her husband, places (gives birth) and re-marries before the vacation of four months and ten (days)’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If her husband who had married her had slept with her, separation would be effected between the two of them and she would observe the waiting period of whatever remained from her first waiting period, and another waiting period from the later one;

and if he had not splet with her, separation would be effected between the two of them and she would observe the waiting period of whatever remained from her waiting period, and he would be a proposer from the proposers’.
en.sarwar: 7. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Safwan ibn Yahya from ibn Muskan from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a pregnant widow who after childbirth marries before the end of four months and ten days.

He (the Imam) said, ‘If the new husband has gone to bed with her he must stay away from her and she must complete the remaining time of the first waiting period and another waiting period for the later (separation).

If he has not gone to bed with her they must separate from each other and she must complete the remaining of the first waiting period and he is then one of those who may propose for marriage.’ ” It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Ja’far ibn Sama’ah and Ali ibn Khalid al-‘Aquliy from Karram from Muhammad ibn Muslim from abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, a similar Hadith.
